channel.description: Latest articles from UK Defence Journal (ukdefencejournal.org.uk)

item.title: No current plans for laser weapons on UK carriers
item.description: The Ministry of Defence has confirmed that there are currently no plans to fit defensive laser weapons directly to the Royal Navy’s aircraft carriers. The post No current plans for laser weapons on UK carriers first appeared on UK Defence Journal.

item.title: Trump unveils new laser battleship named after himself
item.description: The planned Trump-class battleships would displace over 35,000 tonnes and combine laser defences, hypersonic and nuclear-capable missiles, railguns and large vertical launch capacity. The post Trump unveils new laser battleship named after himself first appeared on UK Defence Journal.

item.title: What do we know about America’s new modern battleship?
item.description: Here are the key specifications of America’s new Trump-class laser-armed battleship, a large guided-missile surface combatant designed for hypersonic strike and nuclear deterrence. The post What do we know about America’s new modern battleship? first appeared on UK Defence Journal.

item.title: Downie presses on Rosyth docking timeline for Dreadnought
item.description: The Ministry of Defence has confirmed that early design work is underway to deliver a Contingent Docking Facility at Rosyth Dockyard, following a parliamentary question from Graeme Downie MP. The post Downie presses on Rosyth docking timeline for Dreadnought first appeared on UK Defence Journal.

item.title: UK confirms carrier drone refuelling still under review
item.description: The Ministry of Defence has confirmed that work on autonomous, carrier-based refuelling and logistics aircraft for the Royal Navy remains ongoing, underlining that no decisions have yet been taken on fielding such systems. The post UK confirms carrier drone refuelling still under review first appeared on UK Defence Journal.

item.title: Challenger 3 production tied to trials, not fixed date
item.description: The Ministry of Defence has confirmed that manufacturing of the Challenger 3 main battle tank will not begin on a fixed timetable, but only once performance trials have been successfully completed. The post Challenger 3 production tied to trials, not fixed date first appeared on UK Defence Journal.

item.title: RAF engineer retention scheme for F-35 costs £113.5m
item.description: The Ministry of Defence has disclosed that the RAF’s Financial Retention Incentive for engineers supporting the UK’s F-35 Lightning programme is worth approximately £113.5 million. The post RAF engineer retention scheme for F-35 costs £113.5m first appeared on UK Defence Journal.

item.title: UK to restart nuclear submarine defuelling in 2026
item.description: The Ministry of Defence has confirmed that defuelling of the UK’s decommissioned nuclear-powered submarines is set to restart in 2026, as preparations continue at specialist dock facilities in Devonport. The post UK to restart nuclear submarine defuelling in 2026 first appeared on UK Defence Journal.

item.title: MOD cites family life and civilian jobs in troop exits
item.description: The Ministry of Defence has said that pressures on family life and opportunities outside the military remain the primary reasons personnel leave the armed forces, despite recent improvements in recruitment and retention. The post MOD cites family life and civilian jobs in troop exits first appeared on UK Defence Journal.

item.title: UK Government has sought ‘legal advice’ on Ajax
item.description: The Ministry of Defence has confirmed that it has sought legal advice from the Government Legal Department on the troubled Ajax armoured vehicle programme, following a direct question from Mark Francois MP. The post UK Government has sought ‘legal advice’ on Ajax first appeared on UK Defence Journal.
